walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 1: Exploratory Portfolio — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 1: Exploratory Portfolio brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 1: Exploratory Portfolio.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?
options: Stippling
Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares

mcqs.q: What can line in a composition imply, even without representing an object?
options: Cool colours like blue.
Movement, direction, emotion, and visual rhythm.
Just measurements.
Only the outline of an object.

mcqs.q: What are the three primary colours in paint (subtractive)?
options: Red, green, and blue.
Black, white, and grey.
Red, yellow, and blue (or magenta, yellow, cyan in print).
Cool colours like blue.

mcqs.q: Which colours typically advance in a composition?
options: Dark colours always advance.
Warm colours (reds, oranges, yellows).
Black, white, and grey.
Cool colours like blue.

Layered hatching at different angles to darken tones.
Continuous line drawn around the edge of a form, without lifting the pencil.
